why_winner: C is the only draft whose first line carries both sides of the comparison, which is the shape every top performer in the tracker shares, and it opens with zero scene-setting. It is also the furthest structurally from the Contrarian post already shipped on this idea.

runner_up_notes.A: The one genuinely first-person line in the whole set is A's 'I was re-onboarding the same new hire every single day and calling it a workflow.' That is the sentence a reader believes. C is entirely third-person and reads slightly like commentary about other people. Graft that admission into C.
runner_up_notes.B: 'None of this needs a better model. It needs an hour of configuration you keep postponing.' is the sharpest cost line in the set. Worth borrowing. B is otherwise penalised on plan_compliance: 'you are using a slice of it' and its feature-list rhythm land very close to the 2026-07-19 post's 'you're using a fraction of it', which the plan explicitly rules out.

issues.description: C states its thesis twice. The opening establishes 'same model, different configuration' and then the penultimate paragraph re-states it as 'the engineer who says AI is overrated and the one who says it changed how they build are usually running the same model.' The second pass adds nothing and softens the close.
issues.action: Cut the restatement. End the body on the cost of not doing it (borrow B's 'does not need a better model, needs an hour of configuration you keep postponing') and go straight into the first-step line.

issues.description: C never puts Altaf in the post. Every claim is about two hypothetical engineers, so the reader has no reason to believe the writer runs this setup, which he does.
issues.action: Graft A's first-person admission in after the day-one analogy: the re-explaining-the-project-every-morning habit, named as re-onboarding the same hire daily. One line, first person, no story detour.

issues.description: 'One of them says AI writes code like their team wrote it. The other says it is fine, but you still have to fix everything.' is two clauses of paraphrased opinion where one concrete contrast would hit harder.
issues.action: Tighten to a single split line so the contrast lands in the first two seconds of the preview text.
